records.name: Zimbabwe
records.summary_text:
Zimbabwe is dangerous for trans visitors. The 2006 Criminal Law Act criminalises sodomy (up to 1 year — a lighter formal penalty than neighbours, though indecency provisions add exposure), and Amnesty's 2024 report documents shrinking civic space threatening LGBT organising (GALZ operates under pressure; its offices have been raided historically). There is no legal gender recognition, political rhetoric is hostile, and mob violence is documented — but prosecution under the sodomy law is rarer than in Zambia, and a small organised community persists openly enough to litigate.

records.name: Malawi
records.summary_text: Malawi is dangerous for trans visitors. The Penal Code criminalises same-sex conduct (up to 14 years) AND Human Dignity Trust lists Malawi as criminalising the gender expression of trans people. A moratorium on prosecutions has held since 2014, but in June 2024 the Constitutional Court upheld the ban — a case brought partly by a local trans woman and her Dutch partner — and religious leaders led nationwide anti-LGBT marches in 2023. Discrimination and violence are regular despite the moratorium.
